newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Life welcomes K&H Bank bid success.
newsitem.headline: Irish Life welcomes K&H Bank bid success.

text.p: Irish Life said on Wednesday that it was delighted with the success of its bid along with Belgium's Kredietbank for a stake in Kereskedelmi Bank (K&H Bank), Hungary's second largest bank.

"For Irish Life this success is particularly significant as it broadens the range of our financial services activities to include retail banking," managing director David Kingston said in a statement.

"This is very much in line with our group strategy to seek opportunities in Ireland and abroad to move beyond the niche life assurance sector into the broader financial services marketplace," he added.
Irish Life said that the consortium would take a combined holding of around 56 percent in K&H Bank for a total investment of $90 million or 60 million Irish pounds.
The cost of the investment will be satisfied in cash and shared equally with Kredietbank.

Irish Life said that K&H was also being financed by means of a convertible, subordinated bond loan of $30 million from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) which would entitle the EBRD to a stake of around 17 percent in the bank upon conversion.
Irish Life and Kredietbank have concluded a shareholders' agreement with the EBRD which will give the consortium the right of first refusal in the event of the disposal of these shares by EBRD.
Irish Life and Kredietbank already jointly own Dublin-based Irish Intercontinental Bank and have mutual shareholdings.
